description: Two canonical-form rules that all three SDKs got wrong in different ways, found by a cross-SDK parity audit of purpose binding. Neither is observable through access decisions -- both produce identical enforcement and differ only in the SIGNED BYTES -- so only a byte comparison across languages could surface them. Canonical spec sections 1 and 14 make identical bytes the requirement, and section 14 recommends comparing bytes rather than signatures for exactly this reason.

rules.why: Python's json.dumps emits `1.0` for a float holding a whole number; .NET's System.Text.Json and JavaScript's JSON.stringify both emit `1`. A policy setting confidenceThreshold to 1.0 or minSimilarityScore to 0.0 -- both schema-valid, both reachable when json.loads produces a float -- therefore signed different bytes in Python than in the other two, and a Python-signed context failed verification in both. Two of three already agreed on the shorter form, so Python moved.
rules.note: A boolean must NOT be shortened to a number. Python's bool is a subclass of int, so a naive numeric coercion turns `true` into `1` -- which would be a second, worse divergence introduced by the fix for the first.

rules.why: An ISO 8601 date-time with no offset and no `Z` was read as LOCAL time by .NET's System.Text.Json and by JavaScript's Date, so the signed bytes depended on the host's timezone -- the same JSON signing to three different instants on three hosts. That is a divergence between two deployments of the SAME SDK, worse than a cross-SDK one, and invisible to any fixture pinned to a single host. Python already assumed UTC, which is the only host-independent reading, so .NET and TypeScript moved. Section 2 rule 4 mandates normalizing to UTC but was silent on what an offset-less value means.

cases.note: no offset: assumed UTC, never local
an explicit offset still names its instant and is honoured
offset-less AND sub-second: both rules apply
a zero fractional part is dropped entirely (section 2 rule 5)

rules.note: Every case MUST produce its stated canonical form under every timezone listed. Running the suite only under UTC -- which CI does -- cannot detect this class of bug, so an SDK asserting these MUST vary TZ explicitly or assert the parse in a way that does not depend on the host clock.
